decisions.reason: Although it disappeared as a distinct website item after 2019, transactional email is highly related to the firm's core messaging knowledge and R&D base, so it is more likely to be retained, possibly as an integrated platform capability rather than a standalone offer.

Document capture and recognition is the least tightly connected to the firm's core communications expertise, and after two years without visible market emphasis the firm would likely reallocate resources to areas where it can learn and improve faster.

Email and fax conversion still fits the firm's multichannel integration capabilities and customer need to bridge legacy and digital workflows, so despite lower prominence it remains worth keeping for now.
A narrow fax optimization feature offers limited strategic learning and weak future leverage compared with broader cloud messaging products, making it a likely candidate for withdrawal.

Threat protection closely matches the firm's secure messaging positioning and can be improved through its in-house R&D, so the missing website visibility is more plausibly integration into the core service than imminent discontinuation.
